body.rationale: Governing IPS is still a draft, so compliance findings are provisional. I weighted IPS compliance, technical errors found by reviewers, and the late-cycle preference for covariance-based methods over return-forecast methods. First: resampled_efficient_frontier. It has no hard IPS breaches, effective N of 13.3, tracking error of 4.33%, and a moderate CRO score of 0.44. Its reviewers found a tuning-description inconsistency and a weakness in the stated confidence weighting, but no structural flaw. Its premise of unbiased CMA noise is the weakest link, though resampling spreads the damage across many draws. Second: black_litterman. It is compliant, has the lowest tracking error among the compliant optimised candidates (3.01%), backtest Sharpe of 0.70, and effective N of 6.1. Its flagged problems are the gamma description and the 8.00% volatility sitting on the floor, which are disclosure issues rather than fatal ones. Third: pc_researcher. Its Sharpe of 0.51 and backtest Sharpe of 0.70 are strong, its drawdown is only -10.9%, and its CRO risk is 0.33. Reviewers did find two technical issues: the stated volatility cap conflicts with the 3.82% result, and the 0.51 Sharpe above max_sharpe's 0.46 needs reconciling. It also breaches the volatility and tracking error limits, so it ranks below the compliant candidates. Fourth: cvar_minimization. It is compliant and has the best backtest Sharpe in the field (0.74) with a -18.7% drawdown. The reviewer called its tail construction correctly applied, though CVaR estimates from about 20 tail months are noisy. It adds a non-traditional diversifier to the ensemble. Fifth: risk_parity. It has covariance-only construction, eff. N of 4.7, volatility of 1.97%, and a CRO score of 0.28, so it fits a late-cycle emphasis on covariance structure. It is the best of the low-vol risk-structured group, but it breaches three IPS limits and its equal risk budget for cash is a design flaw. Why first beats fifth: resampled_efficient_frontier is CIO-ready as-is, with no IPS breach, return near 7.1%, volatility in band and wide diversification. risk_parity is a defensive building block that fails return, volatility and tracking error. Bottom flag: hierarchical_risk_parity. It is 91.9% cash, 1.4 effective assets, 0.65% volatility, and Sharpe 0.14, the weakest in the field. Two reviewers (intra-category maximum_diversification and an inter-category one) documented the cash degeneracy, and it breaches three IPS limits, so the CIO should not lean on it. I did not flag adversarial_diversifier because its orthogonality is useful in an ensemble. I excluded market_cap_weight because of its -40.6% drawdown and 0.80 CRO risk.
